raw_response:
I've been farming these 5 mu in Quzhou for 26 years now. My father taught me, and over time I've learned what this soil will give me. I'm 46, my wife and I do most of the work, and my son works off-farm in the city — sends a bit back, which helps, but I still need the land to feed us and bring cash.

This year I'll keep it simple. Spring maize is my main crop — it's reliable and doesn't need the constant attention that vegetables do. I'll put 3.5 mu into maize and plant in late April once the frost risk is past. I'll buy hybrid seed from the county supply shop like I've done for the last 15 years. My neighbor down the road tried saving his own maize seed and his yield dropped badly — I'm not making that mistake.

For the remaining 1.5 mu I'll plant kidney beans in early May. Beans bring good money per mu and my family eats them too. I use improved variety seed for the beans — not the most expensive hybrid, but better than the old saved seeds I used when I was young.

Fertilizer — I apply what I know works. For maize I put down base fertilizer before planting and top-dress with urea when the plants are knee-high. I figure about 16 kg of nitrogen per mu for the maize, and maybe 6 kg of phosphorus and 5 kg of potassium. The beans don't need as much nitrogen — they fix some themselves — so I'll give them about 12 kg nitrogen, 5 kg phosphorus, and 5 kg potassium per mu.

I have a well, so I irrigate when the crops need it. Maize gets thirsty at jointing and grain-filling, so I'll water it about 3 times. The beans I'll irrigate 3 times too, especially when they're flowering.

For pests, I keep an eye on the fields and spray when I see problems. Maize usually needs 2 rounds — once for weeds early, once for borers later. Beans are easier, maybe 1 or 2 sprays if the aphids show up.

I use rotary tillage — I rent the small tractor from the village cooperative. It's what I can afford and it works fine on my small plot.

I expect about 480 kg per mu from the maize if the weather cooperates, and maybe 5,000 kg per mu from the kidney beans.
